set.body:
MEASURED, not reasoned. First slice of bd-01M19N0W937KVZCK78F6X57X1D (enumerate constructible product types WITH INVARIANTS). I filtered the 422 parameterised enum cases to the 12 carrying a Double, then read each for an invariant construction could violate. KernelShape is the one that bites.

  NANBW Rectangular isPointMass=false w(0)=0.0 w(1)=0.0  passesValid=TRUE  TRUE
  NANBW Triangular  isPointMass=false w(0)=NaN w(1)=NaN  passesValid=false false
  NANBW Gaussian    isPointMass=false w(0)=NaN w(1)=NaN  passesValid=false false
  NANBW control Gaussian(1.0) w(0)=1.0 w(1)=0.6065306597126334

THE DESIGN IS MOSTLY RIGHT, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS SUBTLE. window.scala guards b <= 0.0 as a DECLARED POINT MASS -- zero and negative bandwidths are intentional and documented, and there is no division by zero. And Sample.hasValidWeight (Estimate.isFinite(weight) && weight >= 0.0) IS enforced, at window.scala:109 and :371. That is the wire-boundary remedy working: a NaN bandwidth reaches Triangular or Gaussian, produces NaN weights, and is REJECTED.

IT IS INCOMPLETE FOR EXACTLY ONE SHAPE. NaN escapes the b <= 0.0 guard (NaN <= 0.0 is false, so isPointMass is false too -- it falls between both intended regimes). Rectangular then evaluates `math.abs(d) <= b`, which with NaN is FALSE FOR EVERY d, returning 0.0. Zero is finite and non-negative, so hasValidWeight PASSES.

CONSEQUENCE: a Rectangular kernel with NaN bandwidth is not rejected and is not a point mass. It is a window in which EVERY WEIGHT IS ZERO, handed to a smoothing reducer as though it were a legitimate window. The reducer sees no support rather than an error.

THIS IS THE UNIFYING DEFECT IN ITS PUREST FORM: a NaN that becomes a ZERO instead of staying a NaN is a value that cannot be told apart from a legitimate zero. Triangular and Gaussian propagate the NaN and get caught precisely BECAUSE arithmetic preserves it; Rectangular uses a COMPARISON, and comparison is where NaN stops being contagious.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND the one shape: the bandwidth also reaches identity. ReducerId is built as kernel-${name}-${CanonicalDouble.render(bw)} via ReducerId.unsafe, and WeightingPolicy.Kernel(name, bw) carries it into published policy.

FIX SHAPES, not decided -- this is features' call:
  (a) treat non-finite bandwidth as invalid at construction (smart constructor returning Either), which makes it an unforgeable-shape type;
  (b) or extend the existing wire boundary: make isPointMass/weight handle non-finite b explicitly rather than letting it fall through the b <= 0.0 test.
(b) is smaller and matches the module's existing style. (a) is stronger but changes a public enum's construction path.

NOT CLAIMING AN INCIDENT: I found no code that constructs a NaN bandwidth. This is a reachable hole, not an observed failure.

Measured by the chief in a clone; LocallyObserved, not Confirmed. The measuring suite is scratch, not committed -- anyone reproducing should write their own rather than trust this note.
set.title: features: KernelShape.Rectangular(NaN) yields an all-zero window that PASSES the weight validity check
